supply arbitrary fromToken, toToken, amount, receiverAddress, swapExtraData

assets.name: SocketGateway ETH balance
assets.location: SocketGatewayTemplate — accumulated from receive(), in-flight msg.value

trustBoundaries.name: delegatecall boundary
trustBoundaries.description: SocketGateway.executeRoute delegatecalls WrappedTokenSwapperImpl; address(this)=SocketGateway, so its ETH balance and token holdings are the ones acted upon.

threats.title: SocketGateway ETH balance drained via attacker-controlled toToken in performAction Native-to-Wrapped path
threats.description: performAction's Native-to-Wrapped branch sends amount ETH from address(this) to toToken via an unrestricted low-level call, then validates the operation by reading toToken.balanceOf(socketGateway) before and after. When executed via delegatecall from SocketGateway, address(this) is SocketGateway, so actual ETH from the Gateway's balance is sent. Both the toToken address and swapExtraData are caller-supplied with no allowlist check. A malicious toToken can spoof balanceOf to make the difference equal amount regardless of reality, and return true from transfer. This lets an attacker drain SocketGateway's pre-existing ETH without sending any ETH themselves.

steps.finding: executeRoute calls addressAt(routeId).delegatecall(routeData) with no access control. In the delegatecall context address(this)=SocketGateway.

fromToken==NATIVE_TOKEN_ADDRESS branch: reads toToken.balanceOf(socketGateway) as initial snapshot, then calls toToken.call{value: amount}(swapExtraData), then reads toToken.balanceOf(socketGateway) again, requires difference==amount, then calls ERC20(toToken).transfer(receiverAddress, amount).

Both balanceOf reads target the attacker-controlled toToken contract. Attacker implements balanceOf to return 0 on the first call and amount on the second, satisfying the require without any real token being minted.

In delegatecall context toToken.call{value: amount} sends amount ETH from SocketGateway to attacker's toToken contract. If attacker sets amount = SocketGateway.balance and msg.value=0, all Gateway ETH is drained at zero attacker cost.

threats.attackScenario:
1. Attacker deploys MaliciousWETH: balanceOf returns 0 on first call, amount on second; transfer returns true; receive() accepts ETH.
2. Attacker calls SocketGateway.executeRoute(wrappedSwapRouteId, performAction(NATIVE_TOKEN_ADDRESS, MaliciousWETH, SocketGateway.balance, attacker, 0, 0x)) with msg.value=0.
3. delegatecall executes performAction with address(this)=SocketGateway.
4. initial snapshot = MaliciousWETH.balanceOf(SocketGateway) = 0.
5. MaliciousWETH.call{value: SocketGateway.balance}(0x) — all ETH leaves SocketGateway.
6. final snapshot = MaliciousWETH.balanceOf(SocketGateway) = SocketGateway.balance (spoofed).
7. require passes. MaliciousWETH.transfer(attacker, amount) returns true.
8. Attacker withdraws ETH from MaliciousWETH.
suggestedProperties: toToken must be validated against a registry of known wrapped-token contracts before the call
swapExtraData should be restricted to a known deposit() selector
amount should equal msg.value, not a free parameter

claimAssessment.executionContext: caller: any unprivileged EOA or contract; storage: address(this)=SocketGateway during delegatecall; socketGateway immutable in impl also equals SocketGateway — both refer to the same address; tokenOwnership: ETH being spent belongs to SocketGateway (address(this).balance in delegatecall); no user approval needed for the native-token path; deploymentAssumptions: WrappedTokenSwapperImpl registered as a route by admin; SocketGateway holds ETH from prior legitimate use

steps.action: Attacker calls SocketGateway.executeRoute(routeId, encodedPerformAction) with msg.value=0, amount=SocketGateway.balance, toToken=MaliciousWETH
steps.expectedResult: executeRoute delegatecalls performAction; no access control blocks the call

steps.action: MaliciousWETH.call{value: amount}(swapExtraData) executes. In delegatecall context, address(this)=SocketGateway, so amount ETH leaves SocketGateway.
steps.expectedResult: SocketGateway's ETH balance is now 0; MaliciousWETH has received amount ETH

steps.action: _finalBalanceTokenOut = MaliciousWETH.balanceOf(socketGateway) — returns amount (spoofed). require((amount - 0) == amount) passes.
ERC20(MaliciousWETH).transfer(attacker, amount) — MaliciousWETH.transfer returns true. Transaction succeeds.
steps.expectedResult: ETH is permanently in attacker-controlled MaliciousWETH. Attacker can withdraw it.

checks.reason: executeRoute has no access control whatsoever — it is external payable with no modifier. Any EOA or contract can call it with any routeId. performAction has no msg.sender restriction. The attacker only needs the routeId for the registered WrappedTokenSwapperImpl, which is discoverable via emitted NewRouteAdded events.

The sole guard is the balance check `require((_finalBalanceTokenOut - _initialBalanceTokenOut) == amount)`. Both reads target the attacker-controlled toToken; the attacker can return any value. There is no allowlist for toToken, no restriction on swapExtraData, and no reentrancy lock. The ETH transfer happens before the check is computed (line 46 transfer, lines 52-57 check), and the malicious contract's receive() can accept ETH without triggering any rollback. No other guard exists in the path.

The attack is a single linear path — no reentrancy is needed. The malicious toToken accepts ETH in receive() without calling back into SocketGateway. Even if it did re-enter, the damage (ETH drained) is already done before the check; reentrancy is unnecessary for the exploit to complete.

Attacker outlay: gas only (msg.value=0). SocketGateway ETH balance before: B. After: 0. MaliciousWETH receives B ETH, attacker withdraws. Attacker net gain = B. Protocol net loss = B. The ERC20(toToken).transfer at line 60 calls the malicious contract which returns true without cost; it does not require any real token from the protocol. The attack creates no offsetting liability.

missingEvidence: Whether any off-chain whitelist or calldata validation layer exists in front of executeRoute (none visible in the on-chain code)
Exact magnitude of SocketGateway's typical in-flight ETH balance

threats.title: Infinite loop in swapAndMultiBridge burns all caller gas and makes function permanently unusable
threats.description: swapAndMultiBridge's first for-loop (lines 121-123) accumulates bridgeRatios but never increments the loop variable index. The condition index < requestLength is permanently true for any non-empty request, causing the loop to spin until the transaction runs out of gas. The function can never succeed or reach the ratio check, the swap, or the bridge calls. Any user who calls it loses their entire gas budget.

steps.finding: for (uint256 index = 0; index < requestLength; ) { ratioAggregate += swapMultiBridgeRequest.bridgeRatios[index]; } — index is declared in the init clause and read inside, but nothing in the loop body or the for statement's update clause increments it.
The second for-loop in the same function correctly has unchecked { ++index; } — confirming the absence in the first loop is an omission, not a design choice.

Every call with requestLength > 0 out-of-gases. No state is mutated before the loop, so no permanent corruption occurs — only guaranteed gas loss. requestLength == 0 would pass the loop but the ratio check (ratioAggregate != CENT_PERCENT) would then revert since 0 != 100e18.

threats.attackScenario:
1. Any user submits swapAndMultiBridge with bridgeRouteIds.length = 1 and any bridgeRatios.
2. Execution enters the first for-loop with index=0, requestLength=1.
3. index is never incremented; loop spins indefinitely.
4. Transaction reverts with out-of-gas. User loses all supplied gas.
5. No privileged access required; any caller can trigger this.
suggestedProperties: First loop must contain unchecked { ++index; } matching the second loop
Integration test: swapAndMultiBridge with length=1 and valid ratios must complete

claimAssessment.executionContext: caller: any unprivileged EOA or contract; storage: no state is written before the loop; no storage corruption results; tokenOwnership: no token transfers occur before the loop; deploymentAssumptions: none beyond the function being present in the deployed SocketGateway

steps.expectedResult: Execution reaches the first for-loop with index=0

steps.action: Loop evaluates: 0 < 1 → true; executes body; index unchanged; 0 < 1 → true; repeats indefinitely
steps.expectedResult: EVM runs out of gas; transaction reverts

steps.action: Compare against second loop which correctly increments index
steps.expectedResult: Confirms the missing increment is an omission; the second loop pattern was the intended design

checks.reason: swapAndMultiBridge is external payable with no access control modifier. Any caller can invoke it. The infinite loop is reached after only the array-length equality check (lines 115-119), which passes for any correctly formed request.

There are no guards between the function entry and the infinite loop. The transaction reverts due to out-of-gas, which does roll back any state — but no state is written before the loop, so rollback provides no protection to the caller. The rollback does prevent partial state corruption but does not prevent the gas loss.
No external calls are made before or during the infinite loop. The loop only reads from calldata (bridgeRatios[index]) and writes to a local variable. No callback surface exists in this path.

This is a DoS/gas-drain, not a token theft. Attacker gains nothing monetarily; the damage is the permanent non-functionality of swapAndMultiBridge and guaranteed gas loss for any caller who attempts to use it.

dismissedCandidates.title: Admin-only function bypass (rescueFunds, rescueEther, killme)
dismissedCandidates.reason: All three functions are guarded by modifiers that check against immutable addresses set at construction. isSocketGatewayOwner reverts if msg.sender != ISocketGateway(socketGateway).owner(); isSocketDeployFactory reverts if msg.sender != socketDeployFactory. No path exists for an unprivileged caller to pass either check.

dismissedCandidates.title: Wrapped-to-Native path arbitrary call profit (fromToken.call(swapExtraData))
dismissedCandidates.reason: In performAction's else-branch the balance check requires address(socketGateway).balance to increase by exactly amount after fromToken.call(swapExtraData). To pass this check without reverting, the attacker's malicious fromToken must send amount ETH back to SocketGateway during the call, costing the attacker amount ETH. The function then immediately sends that same amount ETH to receiverAddress (attacker-controlled). Net is a wash; no ETH is extracted beyond what the attacker funded.

dismissedCandidates.title: Price manipulation / flash loan / constant-product invariant violation
dismissedCandidates.reason: This is a 1:1 wrap/unwrap router with no reserves, no price curve, and no LP positions. The strict equality check (difference == amount) prevents partial fills. There is no spot price to manipulate.
